paragraph:
Methods & Meanings: MEASUREMENT IN DIFFERENT DIMENSIONS
Measurements of length are measurements in one dimension. They are labeled as cm, ft, km, etc.
Measurements of area are measurements in two dimensions. They are labeled as cm^2, ft^2, or square centimeters, square feet, etc. The abbreviation “cm^2” is read as “square centimeters” and not as “centimeters squared.”
1 in × 1 in = 1 in^2
Measurements of volume are measurements in three dimensions. They are labeled as cm^3, ft^3, or cubic centimeters, cubic feet, etc. Read “ft^3” as “cubic feet,” not as “feet cubed.”
1 in × 1 in × 1 in = 1 in^3
gemini_reasoning: This is a reference box ('Methods & Meanings') defining units in different dimensions. While it specifies how to read notation (e.g., 'not as centimeters squared'), it provides direct instruction on convention rather than warning against a common student error.
gpt_oss_or_reasoning: The paragraph warns readers not to misread unit abbreviations (e.g., cm^2), which is a typical mistake students make.
